tablet.name: Zoroastrian (Qadimi) Calendar
tablet.method: Qadimi (Kadmi) reckoning: a fixed 365-day year (12 months of 30 days + 5 Gatha days), no leap day, epoch 16 June 632 CE Julian (accession of Yazdegerd III). Like the Egyptian civil calendar, this wanders against the solar year by about 1 day every 4 years. Shahanshahi also uses a wandering 365-day year; its modern dates fall 30 days later than Qadimi. Fasli uses leap days to keep seasonal alignment. Those two variants are not calculated here. Days within each month are numbered; the five year-end Gatha days are named.

browser.name: ZOROASTRIAN (YAZDEGERDI) CALENDAR
browser.method: Traditional (Qadimi) reckoning: a fixed 365-day year (12 months of 30 days + 5 Gatha days), no leap day, epoch 16 June 632 CE Julian (accession of Yazdegerd III). Like the Egyptian civil calendar, this wanders against the solar year by about 1 day every 4 years; the Fasli and Shahanshahi variants (which apply corrections to stay seasonally aligned) are not implemented. Per-day names within the month are not shown (see source comment for why).
